remove live detatching of volumes from vm instances? it only works well on fedora. support on ubuntu 16.04 is unstable. ciao currently supports live attaching and detaching of volumes. this issue questions whether we should keep the live detaching of volumes feature. the reasons to remove it being: it only really works well on fedora. support on ubuntu 16.04 is flaky. live detaching sometimes fails and needs to be retried. this flakyiness can lead to bat test failures as this feature is tested by bat. live detach doesn't work at all on clearlinux. the qmp command we use to implement this feature is experimental. we don't have any real use case for this feature right now. it could lead to data loss if the vm is writing to the volume when it is detached by controller. the feature adds complexity to launcher and bat which is currently hard to justify. we could remove live detach but keep live attach and detach from stopped volumes.

two identical parse requests can return different results fix for unstable testrecursive test on windows guys, i found one really weird big in bblfsh. i think it is related to daemon itself but cannot be 100% sure. so do not hesitate to move this issue if i am wrong. context machine learning team really want to have reproducible results everywhere where it is possible. so we fix all random seeds to have a deterministic code. suddenly we find out that two identical runs of style-analyzer quality estimation give different results: src-d/style-analyzer 557 . clues lead to bblfsh and i was able to reproduce the bug without our code. let me show you. how to reproduce run in bash docker run -d rm name style analyzer bblfshd privileged -p 9432 \: 9432 \ bblfsh/bblfshd \: v2.11.0 log-level debug docker exec style analyzer bblfshd bblfshctl driver install \ javascript docker://bblfsh/javascript-driver \: v2.6.0 clone repo with data git clone git checkout 6f0a10ec586cfa1a22218b6778bf9c1572b97912 also checked for v1.2.0 driver version. run in python3 from collections import defaultdict import pickle import time import os import bblfsh bc = bblfsh . bblfshclient ( "localhost:9432" ) res = defaultdict ( lambda : defaultdict ( int )) times = defaultdict ( list ) iter n = 10 for i in range ( iter n ): for ( dirpath , dirnames , filenames ) in os . walk ( "telescope" ): for filename in filenames : try : t start = time . time () filepath = os . path . join ( dirpath , filename ) if ".git" in filepath : continue resp = bc . parse ( filename = filepath ) if len ( res [ filepath ]) 0 and resp . status not in res [ filepath ]: print ( "iter %.3d new status %d for filepath %s. counter: %s " % ( i + 1 , resp . status , filepath , dict ( res [ filepath ]))) res [ filepath ][ resp . status ] += 1 times [ filepath ]. append ( time . time () - t start ) except exception as e : print ( filepath , e ) res [ filepath ][ repr ( e )] += 1 i do not think it is important but bblfsh package version is 2.12.6 . my output head telescope/resources/.ds store content must be utf-8, ascii or base64 encoded telescope/resources/.ds store content must be utf-8, ascii or base64 encoded iter 003 new status 2 for filepath telescope/webpack.mix.js. counter: {0: 2} telescope/resources/.ds store content must be utf-8, ascii or base64 encoded telescope/resources/.ds store content must be utf-8, ascii or base64 encoded iter 004 new status 2 for filepath telescope/resources/js/routes.js. counter: {0: 3} iter 004 new status 2 for filepath telescope/resources/js/base.js. counter: {0: 3} how to interpret mainly, if you see the message, that some file gets a new status that means that during the identical requests bblfsh return different statuses. for example, for telescope/webpack.mix.js and telescope/resources/js/routes.js it was able to parse file first but not the second time. notes if you set iter n to bigger number you get much more output messages. sometimes performance for big iter n become super bad. can be related to perf: bblfshd 2.9 non responsive after parsing 1000+ files bblfshd 226 if you feed only js files it works great and always parse them for iter n=100 . so it is important for ml team to have reproducible output from bblfsh. please tell me if you are able to reproduce the issue or need more info from my side.

ensure kubernetes caches don't expire if they are being read by jsoriano make sure kubernetes caches do not expire if they are being read some metrics in metricbeat kubernetes module are cached during a time, if they are not updated they are removed. but it is usual to have pods or containers that are not updated during more time that the expiration cache. current implementation was not renovating expiration times for cache entries so all were eventually removed if updates for them are not received. replace it with the cache implementation available in libbeat, but keeping the existing interface. also, use slashes instead of dashes to generate unique container uids. dashes can be used by kubernetes names, what could lead to ambiguous keys for the caches. fix 10658

make e2e test runner retry commands that fail while a cluster is starting up the queryserver is initialized before the tm node has been properly initialized and queries attempt to access application state before the tm node has called application.beginblocke loaded application state we've got some flaky e2e tests (like coin) that fail every so often due to what i suspect is a timing issue. my theory is that the queryserver starts up before the tm node has properly initialized and queries attempt to access app state before the tm node has called application.beginblock and loaded the app state. so we may need to fix queryserver to return some kind of "not ready" error from endpoints that require access to the app state. then the e2e test runner should auto-retry any command that errors out with "not ready".

git rename and copy detection flaky git does not track file renames or copies the issue git itself doesn't track renames or file copies. even when using git mv it internally still added the content of that file to the new filename and removed the old file. having set that, it's possible to tell git to try to find copies or file moves. for this it uses heuristics, which hunks of which files are identical. if a file is moved without changed contend, git tells 'r100' (r for rename), which mean that the stated files have 100% content in common. since this is a heuristic this can go wrong. see the following example: $ mkdir git log bug $ cd git log bug $ git init initialized empty git repository in /users/user/repos/git log bug/.git/ (master) $ echo "hello world
hello universe" first file.txt (master) $ echo "hello world
hello universe" second file.txt (master) $ git add first file.txt second file.txt (master) $ git commit -m "initial commit" [master (root-commit) b996586] initial commit 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-) create mode 100644 first file.txt create mode 100644 second file.txt (master) $ git rm first file.txt rm 'first file.txt' (master) $ echo "hello some more" second file.txt (master) $ git mv second file.txt renamed second file.txt (master) $ git add renamed second file.txt (master) $ git commit -m "second commit" [master f11add4] second commit 2 files changed, 1 insertions(+), 1 deletions(-) rename first file.txt = renamed second file.txt (63%) delete mode 100644 second file.txt so far so good. runing a git log name-status without copy or rename detection yields the following (simplified): (master) $ git log name-status commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 author: alex date: mon sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit d first file.txt a renamed second file.txt d second file.txt now with rename and copy detection it states this (simplified): (master) $ git log name-status -c -m commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 author: alex date: mon sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit r063 first file.txt renamed second file.txt d second file.txt (master) $ git show -c -m f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 author: alex date: mon sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit diff git a/first file.txt b/renamed second file.txt similarity index 63% rename from first file.txt rename to renamed second file.txt index 7894def..194ec9c 100644 a/first file.txt +++ b/renamed second file.txt @@ -1 +1,2 @@ hello world
hello universe +hello some more diff git a/second file.txt b/second file.txt deleted file mode 100644 index 7894def..0000000 a/second file.txt +++ /dev/null @@ -1 +0,0 @@ so all in all, it detects the wrong file renamed! now this could be ok, if it's consistend. the situation but this is not consistend: cvsanaly itself uses the flages -m and -c for rename and copy detection. the extension commitloc only uses -m (aka find-renames , in my tests -c didn't made a difference) and patches are also generated using find-renames ( patchloc , hunks and indirectly hunkblame uses those patches). since they don't always match this sometimes yield to file id for some-renamed.file @ 1234 not found the solution? one thing could be to enable copy detection on patch creation to patch cvsanaly and all the results of the patch creation. whit this hunks of copied files essentially would be empty. but with this the file id should always be findable. @lewisham and @linzhp : what do you think? ps: this is related to

python thrift caching issue with included thrift files python thrift caching issue with included thrift files test case available on the thrift-include branch of problem under-invalidation when modifying transitive thrift dependencies of a thrift target. we have a thrift api in a.thrift that imports b.thrift and c.thrift . b and c are consumable via separate targets as well. a depends on b and c in the build file in addition to importing them: python thrift library( name='a', sources=[ 'a.thrift', ], dependencies=[ ':b', ':c', ] ) python thrift library( name='b', sources=[ 'b.thrift', ] ) python thrift library( name='c', sources=[ 'c.thrift', ] ) the most reliable reproducer i can find is in a project with artifact caching enabled, make a change to c.thrift and run/build a python target that depends on a.thrift . the changes won't be picked up unless you clean-all . setup clone the repository ./pants binary src/python:test && dist/test.pex expected output: ['c', 'read', 'thrift spec', 'validate', 'write'] uncomment lines 5-7 in src/thrift/c.thrift ./pants binary src/python:test && dist/test.pex expected output ['c', 'cba', 'cfoo', 'cfoobar', 'read', 'thrift spec', 'validate', 'write'] actual output ['c', 'read', 'thrift spec', 'validate', 'write'] if you run ./pants clean-all , you get the expected output, which makes me think this is an artifact caching issue. the actual problem we're seeing in production is even stranger: the addition of a new type to the equivalent of the c.thrift file doesn't get included in the built pex.

fio: pre-filling the attached disk does not work fio: pre-filling the attached disk does not work look at the fio benchmark.prepare() method: fill size = str(disk usable space fraction 1000 disk.disk size) + 'm' let's say that disk.disk size is 3 and disk usable space fraction is 0.9. fill size will be exactly 2700.0m . this format is not accepted by fio and as a result, pre-filling the scratch volume will not work. what is worse, fio command will fail with exit code=0 and we will not even see that something went wrong. my proposition would be: convert fill size to int before converting it to str (format like 2700m is accepted by fio) add more logging around fio command as it sometimes exits without error code.

[py3] top file merge order is variable instead of lexicographical this will affect the expected order of key files and environments. description of issue/question the order that top files are merged in by default has changed when running salt with python 3. we have a couple of tests to check for this - the expected way that top files will be merged/ordered by default is lexicographically when running salt in python 2. python 3 seems to treat lists more as traditional lists - they are unordered and results will vary. i tried to track this down, but the solution isn't immediately apparent to me. i think the problem has something to do with our defaultordereddict class and the way it is instantiated in the get tops function where we instantiate the default factory as a list , but i am just guessing. that might be a red herring. either way, this will affect the expected ordering of top files and environments and will be a regression for people when they switch to python 3. setup i found this issue when running the highstateconf unit tests with python 3. steps to reproduce issue set up the test suite to run with python 3 and run: python3 tests/runtests.py -n unit.highstateconf test there will be two test failures: test basic merge and test ordered merge . these fail because the order of the top files in the merge tops and get tops function calls is now variable and unordered. in python 2, these lists were always ordered lexicographically, and the assertequal would pass. versions report develop branch: salt versions salt version: salt: 2016.3.0-1055-g0329f57 dependency versions: cffi: 0.8.6 cherrypy: 5.0.1 dateutil: 2.4.2 gitdb: 0.6.4 gitpython: 1.0.1 ioflo: 1.5.5 jinja2: 2.8 libgit2: not installed libnacl: not installed m2crypto: 0.21.1 mako: not installed msgpack-pure: not installed msgpack-python: 0.4.6 mysql-python: 1.2.3 pycparser: 2.10 pycrypto: 2.6.1 pygit2: not installed python: 2.7.6 (default, jun 22 2015, 17:58:13) python-gnupg: 0.3.8 pyyaml: 3.10 pyzmq: 14.5.0 raet: not installed smmap: 0.9.0 timelib: 0.2.4 tornado: 4.2.1 zmq: 4.0.5 system versions: dist: ubuntu 14.04 trusty machine: x86 64 release: 4.5.5-x86 64-linode69 system: linux version: ubuntu 14.04 trusty ping @cachedout @thatch45 and @meggiebot

issue 20553 - win acl can't set perms on "c:\program files" due to a… by jimficarra win acl can't set perms issue type bugfix pull request component name win acl ansible version ansible 2.3.0 (devel 06e30485ea) last updated 2017/01/16 20:03:34 (gmt +000) config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg configured module search path = [u'/usr/share/custom modules'] this has existed in this module in previous 2.x releases as well. i confirmed that this is an issue in the latest devel branch as of this writing. summary fixes issues 20553 and 15737 setting permissions where all application packages group applied fails (windows 2012) the security.principal.ntaccount for application package authority\all application packages can't be translated to its sid (security.principal.securityidentifier). this is an issue with the win32 api and is reproducible using powershell and other tools like sysinternals psgetsid. this issue and its resolution (workaround) has been documented on several blogs. [bug] when fully qualifed, all application packages throws "no mapping between account names and security ids was done" chef/win32-security 6 this issue occurs on directories where this built-in account is applied in windows 2012 such as the following dirs: c:\program files c:\program files (x86) c:\windows i went through microsoft's list of well-known sids to see if there were other accounts that could not map to their sid using their fully qualified name, but this is the only one that does not map from ntaccount to securityidentifier. there were some sids that didn't exist in my environment so i could not test them. the fix instantiates a new ntaccount object using the short name in the constructor so the mapping to the sid can be done. error: set-acl : the security identifier is not allowed to be the owner of this object. this issue occurs when the user executing the module from the control server attempts to set permissions using win acl on the target directory when owned by a group in which the user is not a member. this issue is partially documented in several blogs, though i dug further and discovered it only seems to manifest itself when using set-acl on a dir where another group you're not in owns it. . at first i used the suggested work-around in the code by replacing $objacl = get-acl $path with $objacl = (get-item $path).getaccesscontrol('access') however it seems .net 4.6.1 apparently nullifies this workaround - after the upgrade to .net 4.6.1 i started to receive the error again. this did not occur pre-4.6.1. to compensate, i opted to create a function where the aces could be extracted from the security descriptor and used in set-acl. this avoids the issue by applying only aces and not any owner information. more meaningful exception messages (not a bug) i took the opportunity to enhance the exception handling so that any errors occurring in powershell are passed through the exception message. the generic messages hid the useful information underneath and was only visible when generating the module and keeping it on the remote target boxes with ansible keep remote files. sample task for all application packages issue create - name: test perms win acl: path: 'c:\program files\test' user: users rights: fullcontrol type: allow state: present before: fatal: [win2012.mycompany.com]: failed! = { "changed": false, "failed": true, "invocation": { "module name": "win acl" }, "msg": "an error occured when attempting to present fullcontrol permission(s) on c:\\program files\\test for users" } the existing exception handling hides the error from powershell, which is exception calling "translate" with "1" argument(s): "some or all identity references could not be translated. after: changed: [win2012.mycompany.com] = { "changed": true, "invocation": { "module name": "win acl" } } the specified acl is set. sample task for set-acl issue before: assign ownership of d:\win acl test to a new empty group before running tasks: - name: test perms win acl: path: 'd:\win acl test' user: guests rights: read type: allow state: present note that for me this works from ansible but fails in powershell. others have reported an error, and i believe this is related. set-acl : the security identifier is not allowed to be the owner of this object. at c:\users\myuser\appdata\local\temp\ansible-tmp-1484854478.89-6843170110905\win acl.ps1:404 char:13 + set-acl $path $objacl + + categoryinfo : invalidoperation: (d:\win acl test:string) [set-acl], invalidoperationexception + fullyqualifiederrorid : system.invalidoperationexception,microsoft.powershell.commands.setaclcommand {"changed":true} after: copying the ace's avoids the issue with attempting to set the owner changed: [win2012.mycompany.com] = { "changed": true, "invocation": { "module name": "win acl" } }

localdate binding doesn't work when mysql server has a different timezone to the client when i save down localdate fields, they are stored in the db as the previous day. eg if i bind 2018-01-10 when i query the db i see 2018-01-09, and when i retrieve it using jdbi i get 2018-01-09. i have a mysql server that is configured with a timezone of utc. my java app has a timezone of "australia/perth". when i save down localdate fields, they are stored in the db as the previous day. eg if i bind 2018-01-10 when i query the db i see 2018-01-09 , and when i retrieve it using jdbi i get 2018-01-09 . here is a simplified example: public interface reportdao { @sqlupdate("insert into report (report date, title) values (:date, :title") void localdate date, @bind("title") string title); @sqlquery("select report date from report") list<localdate getalldates(); } and this is used as follows: // ... final reportdao verdictdao = jdbi.ondemand(reportdao.class); localdate d = localdate.of(2018, month.january, 10); reportdao.insert(d, "bar"); reportdao.getalldates().foreach(system.out::println); 2018-01-09 is printed, when i expect it to print out 2018-01-10 . client set-up: timezone australia/perth jdbi v3.6.0 mysql-connector-java v8.0.11 (using driver: com.mysql.cj.jdbc.driver) server set-up: timezone utc mysql 5.7.25-0ubuntu0.18.04.2 column type either date, or datetime the problem occurs because the mysql driver will convert the java.sql.date from the client timezone to the server timezone. this seems like the correct thing to do, generally. here is where jdbi interacts with the mysql driver, in javatimeargumentfactory line 29: register(localdate.class, types.date, (p, i, v) - p.setdate(i, java.sql.date.valueof(v))); and in the mysql driver, in clientpreparedquerybindings (called from clientpreparedstatement ), we see this: // jdbi calls the 2-arg setdate() @override public void setdate(int parameterindex, date x) { setdate(parameterindex, x, this.session.getserversession().getdefaulttimezone()); } @override public void setdate(int parameterindex, date x, timezone tz) { if (x == null) { setnull(parameterindex); } else { if (this.ddf == null) { this.ddf = new simpledateformat("''yyyy-mm-dd''", locale.us); } this.ddf.settimezone(tz); setvalue(parameterindex, this.ddf.format(x)); // todo set mysqltype? } } i've tested the above scenario with postgresql and it doesn't suffer from the same issue. i can think of 2 possible fixes for this in the jdbi source: 1. pin the time-zone by supplying a calendar to the setdate() call, in javatimeargumentfactory // calendar.getinstance() pins the client-side timezone thereby avoiding conversion register(localdate.class, types.date, (p, i, v) - p.setdate(i, java.sql.date.valueof(v), calendar.getinstance())); 2. supply an iso date string instead of the date, in javatimeargumentfactory // send the string to the db, and allow the db to coerce it into a date register(localdate.class, types.date, (p, i, v) - p.setdate(i, v.tostring())); i've tested 1. on both mysql and postgresql and it works. it is a bit horrible to create a calendar though. i haven't tested 2. but it should work. especially, given that both mysql and postgresql drivers format the date as a string before sending to the servers. 2. is flaky though, as i'm pretty sure oracle allows a date format to be set per session. so there's a good chance that this will not work in systems not using iso formats. please let me know if you'd like more info!

ui-sortable + ng-repeat has flaky behavior on drag & drop ui-sortable + ng-repeat has flaky behavior on drag & drop when you use ui-sortable with ng-repeat it does not work properly on drag & drop. the reason for this is that the call to element.sortable(opts); in the bottom of the link-function is triggered before the elements have rendered as html (this can easily be shown by adding an alert('link') right before or after the call. at that point you can see that the elements from ng-repeat are not there. if you wrap this call in a timeout of 100 (maybe less, but i'll stick to 100) it works, because then the elements are actually on the page. the following is a demonstration of a sortable list that has actual written html (top) and one that is generated through ng-repeat (bottom). as mentionened above, the fix for this bug would be to implement a timeout when initializing sortable. also, you will have to put the top part (the whole part of if (ngmodel)) in an init function, otherwise they will not work properly. $timeout(function () { initsortable(); element.sortable(opts); }, 100);

fix collabedit race condition it doesn't handle any failures on either side via retries or otherwise. i.e. if one client fails to send up a diff, the loop stalls. collabedit is acting very flaky in my testing on the ui branch right now. i'm seeing behaviour where the application only works 30% of the time. a brief recap of what actually happens in the collabedit loop on the server side: wait for two clients to join. do nothing till then upon the second client joining, start the sync loop ask the first client for its diff send this diff down to the second client ask the second client for its diff send this diff down to the first client return to step 3 the one issue with this already is that it doesn't handle any failures on either side via retries or otherwise. i.e. if one client fails to send up a diff, the loop stalls. a second issue is with timing on the part of the second client. basically, on the client side, each client sets up its collabeditview and subsequently subscribes to a couple of events on the eventbus pertaining to the synchronization loop. the problem we're having is that the server has already completed step 5 of its loop and is waiting for the second client to send up the diff, but the second client hasn't finished subscribing to the events from the bus, so it's not able to respond with a diff, thereby halting our collabedit loop. an interesting observation is that we don't have this issue in the current version of the code on develop. my hypothesis is that with the existing code, there is no extra rendering taking place for the textarea since it's directly entered in the html. in my ui branch, i have react rendering our textbox, which is much slower than the browser just parsing html and doing the render. this extra time leads to a delay in the collabeditview and the event subscription. to fix this, i propose some kind of collabedit setup, similar to the interview setup we have using the init interview message type. using this, the server can be absolutely sure that both clients are ready to send up their diffs before asking for them. further, if we add some sort of retry mechanism, we can greatly improve the overall reliability of the system

only run piggybacked operations after sr is finished, and isolate them by leastbad there could be a race condition where piggybacked operations might start running before sr operations are completed type of pr (feature, enhancement, bug fix, etc.) bug fix description piggybacked operations would run for all tabs, which is a problem for isolation mode. also, there could be a race condition where piggybacked operations might start running before sr operations are completed. this pr fixes both issues. post-script this ended up being a lot more involved than i originally anticipated. the primary change ended up requiring that i modify the method missing in cable ready channels.rb so that the reflex id is added to the options for every operation. the client then compares the reflexid attached to the operation against the reflexes dictionary to decide whether it should be executed on the current tab context. it seems like a viable solution but there could be cases i haven't considered. would appreciate more brains on this. i've spent the last few hours attempting to isolate and address a 2nd race condition that emerged when sending cr broadcasts inside a reflex. it seems like the path to cableready.perform(data.operations) on line 105 of reflexes.js is super short, right? not only is the websocket message with the cr broadcast sent before the morph broadcast, but the reflexoperations on line 101 kicks off a multi-stage process involving several events and potentially dom updates... and yet! somehow, the question of whether line 101 or 105 fires first is non-deterministic. i'm at a complete loss to explain this phenomena. apparently object.entries (line 104) is slow, but it was happening even when i commented out line 104... and come on, it's not that slow. still, you can't argue with observable, repeatable observations. if i wrap line 101 in a settimeout(,5) the problem goes away about 99% of the time, although i still saw 1-2 show up out of order. as of right now, i've taken this as far as i can. what i plan to tell people is that if the order of operations is critcal, eg. that it must be cableready broadcasts morphs cableready operations that piggyback on the morphs ... then they should follow their cable ready calls with a sleep 0.01 to sleep 0.1 so that the cableready broadcasts have a good chance to finish before the morph returns. in other words, this will work: def test cable ready . console log ( message : "am i before the morph, or after?" ) . broadcast morph :nothing end but if you need to guarantee that the console log executes before the morph returns, you're looking at: def test cable ready . console log ( message : "definitely before the morph" ) . broadcast sleep 0.01 morph :nothing end in order to make this work reliably without sleep calls (although still non-deterministically ordered) i had to go ahead and comment out (former) line 74 of lifecycle.js which removed completed reflexes from the reflexes dictionary. this is something i already planned to do in the next major version of the library, and there's no obvious downside although long-running applications might start to occupy memory if lots of reflexes are used. (the plan is for the next major version to have a reaping strategy, sort of like how redis has a key expiration strategy. hopefully, this will be fine without reaping until the next version is ready.) final thing: in channel.rb on line 100 i added a safe navigation operator to the reflex logger print statement. this means developers will be able to suppress server-side logging for a single reflex if their reflex action method contains @logger = nil . why should this be added race issues are bad. checklist my code follows the style guidelines of this project checks (standardrb & prettier-standard) are passing this is not a documentation update

resource crud race condition cypress tests running so fast, we actually can see a race condition that can sometimes cause tests to act non-deterministically describe the bug a clear and concise description of what the bug is. currently, upon deletion of a resource (query to delete /api/resources/:id ), we make a call out to get all resources get /api/resources/:id . however, with cypress tests running so fast, we actually can see a race condition that can sometimes cause tests to act non-deterministically, which is a result of the following happening: delete /api/resources/:id call occurs. delete call finishes, api request goes out to get /api/resources/ which gets all resources. while get /api/resources/ is pending, the button is clicked which triggers a get /api/resources/filter query. if /api/resources/filter returns after /api/resources/ , the result of the filter will be populated in the search results. if the opposite happens, all resources will populate the search results. the latter case is causing tests to fail (rightfully so). we can remedy by disabling the search button until requests finish loading as an option, or another option would be to look into redux-observable which allows for automatic request cancellation. or we could just not do the request for all resources after a delete. expected behavior: race condition: api resource filter returns before get /api/resources/ despite being called after. linked to 199 .

integration tests fail non-deterministically when friendbot stopped responding, and again when testnet reset. the functions called are tested with mocked functions in unit tests (and if they aren't, they can and should be). so it's not super helpful to have tests that fail non-deterministically. describe the bug tests will fail, not because the library is broken but because of outside factors. that results in false negatives that can be hard to debug. for example, if friendbot is down or lagging, it'll cause the server integration tests to fail (because the test account will get a 400 error when it tries to fund itself.) some potential fixes: mock responses to all external calls get rid of integration tests; the underlying library calls being tested can be unit-tested make friendbot more resilient

reference counted cache entries by serprex removed the shard id hash in metadata cache.c to simplify cache management, but we observed a significant performance regression that was being masked by the performance improvement provided by 3654 in our benchmarks, but 3654 only applies to specific workloads. addresses issue as outlined in 3688 (comment) this change updates citustablecacheentry to be reference counted. see code in postgres handing domainconstraintcache in typcache.c for inspiration. references themselves are currently leaked until their memory context is destroyed, i think it'd be possible to avoid that by having each reference exist in a child memory context, but postgres doesn't seem to have lightweight memory contexts this makes it so that if a lookup updates a cache entry, out of band data isn't freed. cache entries will not mutate after being looked up fixes 3581 click to expand old text this pr isn't really meant to be merged, as i put it together to see how ugly would it be to throw assertions on top of what we currently have as opposed to coming up with something else. as such i didn't give complete care to handling, error handling in particular looking for more situations like 3670 hadi moshayedi noticed insert-select logic had rather long lived usage of cache entries. this brought about some discussion that essentially concluded that it's invalid to have two live pointers from the metadata cache at any time. this commit found a couple cases where this happens anytime acceptinvalidationmessages is called, we should have no live pointers from the cache. this is called whenever one looks up an entry from the cache one suggestion is that we should instead return copies by-value when looking up cache entries. then it's only a matter of the content becoming stale

deqna/delqa emulation sets incorrect lengths for receive if multiple descriptors are used for a packet. incorrect lengths for receive if multiple descriptors summary the deqna/delqa sets the data length into receive buffer descriptors as '(data transferred for this descriptor' - 60 ). this is the correct value (once software has added back the 60) if the data all relates to a single descriptor, but not if multiple descriptors are used for a packet. the data length value should (i think) simply be the number of bytes transferred into the receive fifo. detail i am just in the process of resurrecting a different release of an old system for which i have had other releases working well under simh. however, the communications in this release did not work. i have tracked it down to the values in the rbl (received byte length) being effectively negative (though in 11 bits). the packets in question are minimum length packets [60 bytes] split into an initial 16 byte buffer for header/protocol information, and with a second large buffer for the remaining maximum packet. reference the deqna user manual states, concerning the two receive status words of the receive buffer descriptor list: receive status word 1 bit definition 10:08 rbl <10:08 . received byte length bits 10 thru 08. see receive status word 2, bits 07:00. these bits are all set during set-up mode packet processing. receive status word 2 this word must be initialized to have unequal high and low bytes. it is then valid when the bytes match. bit definition 15:08 rbl <07:00 . receive byte length bits 07 through 00. duplicated from lower byte. 07:00 rbl <07:00 . receive byte length bits 07 through 00. these bits and receive status word 1 bits 10:08 (above) form rbl <10:00 , the number of bytes transferred into the receive fifo. software adds 60 to this value, to account for the period during which address filtering occurs. the 4-byte crc is not included in the count; crc is not transferred to the fifo. code, and what it does the code extract below is commented to show the resulting arithmetic. the buffer length for the first buffer is obtained [16] / decode buffer length - two's complement (in words) / w length = xq- var- rbdl buf[3] + 1; b length = w length 2; the packet length is obtained, rbl is set to 60, 'used' starts off at zero. item = &xq- var- readq.item[xq- var- readq.head]; rbl = (uint16)item- packet.len; rbuf = item- packet.msg; if (item- packet.oversize) rbuf = item- packet.oversize; / see if packet must be size-adjusted or is splitting / if (item- packet.used) { uint16 used = (uint16)item- packet.used; rbl -= used; rbuf = &rbuf[used]; ... / make sure entire packet fits in buffer - if not, will need to split into multiple buffers / if (rbl b length) rbl = b length; item- packet.used += rbl; ... xq- var- rbdl buf[4] = 0; switch (item- type) { ... case eth itm normal: / normal packet / rbl -= 60; / keeps max packet size in 11 bits / the above sets rbl to -44, 0xffd4 xq- var- rbdl buf[4] = (rbl & 0x0700); / high bits of rbl / xq- var- rbdl buf[4] = 0x00f8; / set reserved bits to 1 / the above sets receive status word 1 to 0x7f8 break; } if (item- packet.used < item- packet.len) xq- var- rbdl buf[4] = xq rst lastnot; / not last segment / this sets rsw1 to 0x17f8 xq- var- rbdl buf[5] = ((rbl & 0x00ff) << 8) (rbl & 0x00ff); this sets rsw2 to 0xd4d4 the code loops for the second descriptor ending up with rsw1 = 0x17f8 and rsw2 = 0xf0f0. note that 60 has been subtracted twice. review so, what should the values be? the deqna manual states these bits [rbl<7:0 ] (received byte length) and receive status word 1 bits 10:08 (above) form rbl <10:00 , the number of bytes transferred into the receive fifo. note that is does not say that it relates to the number of bytes transferred into the respective buffers. the system driver in use has no code for handling negative values, so i believe that the value is unsigned and positive, and that it is likely that for a minimum length packet, both buffer descriptors should be given an entry of value zero. this is supported by the fact that the driver adds 46. to the rbl value. (though i have not yet figured out why it is not 44.) this gives the size of the packet contents, not the overall size. the 16 header bytes are kept separately. debug output dbgextract.txt solution i changed pdp11 xq.c as follows from rbl -= 60; / keeps max packet size in 11 bits / to rbl = item- packet.len - 60; / the number of bytes transferred into the receive fifo / the system is still mildly flaky when i stress it, but before this change, it just threw away all incoming packets. the solution for the flakiness may just be configuration of enough buffers, so i'm not too worried. version sim sho version pdp-11 simulator v4.0-0 beta simulator framework capabilities: 32b data 32b addresses threaded ethernet packet transports:pcap:nat:udp idle/throttling support is available virtual hard disk (vhd) support raw disk and cd/dvd rom support asynchronous i/o support asynchronous clock support frontpanel api version 4 host platform: compiler: microsoft visual c++ 15.00.30729.01 simulator compiled as c arch: x86 (release build) on feb 11 2017 at 10:52:53 memory access: little endian memory pointer size: 32 bits large file ( 2gb) support sdl video support: sdl version 2.0.5 pcre regex support for expect commands os clock resolution: 1ms time taken by msleep(1): 1ms os: microsoft windows [version 10.0.16299.431] architecture: x86 on amd64, processors: 2 processor id: amd64 family 16 model 4 stepping 3, authenticamd, level: 16, revision: 0403 git commit id: bce72b2 how you built the simulator or that you're using prebuilt binaries the above was a pre-built binary. i have also cloned and used the current source code from github (13th may 2018), built under visual studio 2015, to debug what was happening.

coprocess test still flakey this is a race condition involving delivery of the sigterm during the really tiny window between all of the work over the past few months has dramatically reduced the flakiness of the ksh unit tests. including the coprocess unit test. i did some controlled experiments and every single time it times out it is the "coprocess 2 hung" case that hangs. i stripped that unit test down to just that test case. that allows the unit test to finish in under 100 ms. which makes it practical to get a handle on the failure rate. on two of my linux vms it averages around one failure per 40 runs. running the hanging cat via strace sems to make it impossible to reproduce the hang. so instead i modified the timeout trap to run gdb on the stuck cat and dump its stack. what we see is this: (gdb) bt 0 0x00007fd24889a320 in read nocancel () from /lib64/libc.so.6 1 0x00000000004055e6 in ?? () 2 0x000000000040275f in ?? () 3 0x00007fd2487da725 in libc start main () from /lib64/libc.so.6 4 0x00000000004028d9 in ?? () bingo! this is a race condition involving delivery of the sigterm during the really tiny window between checking if a cancelation is pending and doing the non-cancellable read. see for lots of gory details. for the life of me i can't figure out what this specific test case is supposed to be testing. it doesn't verify that the cat actually reads and writes the test data. it's only testing that a background process can be killed. the part which tests we can inject data into the pipe for the co-process to read is already verified by other test cases. so this test case really has nothing to do with testing the coprocess functionality; or at least doesn't add anything not already done by other tests. the fix is to close the write side of the co-process pipe so that the read done by cat returns eof.

fix memory leak in singleton object pool by mxz297 my experience is that memory usage of code parsing for a binary with 170mb .text size decreased from 12.0gb to 9.3gb on x86. the impact on power or arm can be larger. i have a run that rans out of memory on zeroah, which has 64gb memory, and now it can finish with about using 7gb memory. two memory leak fixes related singleton object pool. the singleon object pool currently only destructs objects but does not deallocate memory space. this leak applies to all architectures. on ppc and arm, instruction decoder does not use smart pointers to manage instructionapi::instruction constructed by a singleon object pool, and thus cause memory leaks.

bug: compatibility with openmp syscalls are called prior to the call to madvise(). ultimately one of the two threads finally calls madvise() and seccomp properly kills that thread. but openmp has synchronization between the threads and before the second thread can call madvise() (and get killed), the second thread calls futex() as it is waiting on something from the dead thread. and this is why the program hangs. one thread has been killed and the second thread is waiting for data (from the dead thread) that will never arrive. the non-deterministic nature of multi-threading makes this one hard to debug, but i think, i have arrived at a rather reproducible test case seccomp omp.c.gz . compile the program with -o0 -ggdb -fopenmp . if we execute it with just one thread and let it do the forbidden syscall, the program dies as expected. $ ./seccomp omp -t 1 -k 0 86195973 [1] 10103 invalid system call (core dumped) ./seccomp omp -t 1 -k 0 however, given more threads it just ceases to function. $ ./seccomp omp -t 2 -k 0 86198868 86195973 86200317 ^c the program doesn't get killed, it just stops doing anything, at all. i am at a loss what happened to the sigsys signal, and why it doesn't get handled? this might not be a libseccomp issue at all, but i am not proficient enough with seccomp, signals and the threading system in general to debug the root cause. hope you can make some sense of it.

tests: new sanitycheck tag "emu time"; increase some timeouts by marc-hb as written originally, the tests assumed that if k uptime get 32() returns times in milliseconds, that it also has millisecond resolution quoting bug "configure qemu to run independent of the host clock 14173 " we have been struggling for years with issues related to how qemu attempts to synchronize guest timer interrupts with the host clock, for example 12553 . the symptom is that heavily loaded sanitycheck runs have tests spuriously failing due to timing related issues. this creates noise in our ci runs which masks true bugs in our system which manifest only intermittently, causing real issues that will happen all the time at scale to be 'swept under the rug'; right now any time a test fails sanitycheck retries it a few times and only consecutive failures produce an error. there's also a lot of relevant information and more links in: "list of tests that keep failing sporadically" 12553 this new "emu time" tag helps by letting users either select or exclude the tests that really need accurate time to pass and have a high chance to actually be impacted by this emulation issue. as an example, it's only with 'sanitycheck exclude emu time' that i could spot and file intermittent but non-emu time issue 16915 . as andrew predicted above, it was drown in emu time noise before that. conversely, " tag emu time" can be used by developers focusing on fixing qemu's -icount feature, for instance 14173 or others. even before qemu's -icount is fixed, continuous integration could be split in two separate runs: a. tag emu time and b. exclude emu time. only a tests would be allowed retries which would stop hiding other, unrelated intermittent issues affecting b tests. this initial commit does not pretend to exhaustively tag all affected tests. however it's an already functional and useful start of 14 tests collected from and tested over weeks of local sanitycheck runs and partially reviewed by qemu clock expert andy ross. this commit also increases the individual timeout of 7 tests that have been observed to consistently take much longer than the median (2-3s). this flags how unusually long these are, lets users temporarily reduce the very long 60s default timeout in their local workspace and finally should reduce the chance of them timing out on a heavily loaded system. set their timeout to 3-4 times the duration observed in ci and locally. signed-off-by: marc herbert

enforce usage of k thread stack sizeof macro in k thread create() downgrading this to low. basically, because it results only in some ram waste for arm, but no serious impact, otherwise. describe the bug there is some inconsistency in how the macros related to thread stack definition are actually user in zephyr applications/samples/tests/subsystems. ideally, we want to define a thread stack object using stack obj = k thread stack define (sym, nominal size ) call k thread create with stack size = k thread stack sizeof(stack obj) in this way we guarantee that k thread stack create is given the amount of stack area (in bytes) that can actually be used by the thread, excluding, for instance, a privileged stack guard (in arm builds). however, this is not always the case: in several cases (including even the main thread) k thread stack create is passed nominal size , instead of k thread stack size of(sym). if privileged stack guards are to be used on arm builds with requirement for power-of-two start/size alignment of stack objects, then this is a bug , because k thread stack define is supplied with a size value that is larger that what the thread can actually use: this is because in that case no extra area is allocated for the guard. in arm builds with config mpu requires power of two alignment && userspace we have a work-around for this, but it effectively eats up 32-bytes from the stack objects. expected behavior always call k thread stack create() with argument stack size = k thread stack sizeof(stack object) , where, stack object = k thread stack define(nominal size) document this properly in the doc

bgsave by jeffreylovitz this is a solution to the problem of bgsave commands hanging indefinitely if invoked while the graph's read-write lock is held this is a solution to the problem of bgsave commands hanging indefinitely if invoked while the graph's read-write lock is held ( ). since bgsave operates on a forked process, if this lock is held when bgsave is called, the bgsave process will never be notified when that lock is released (this is thread data, not process data). i don't love this solution. it gets the job done, but causes bgsave to block until it can acquire all locks, which contradicts the point of the call. it additionally seems very possible to me that enterprise environments fork for reasons other than bgsaves, which would cause a lot of unnecessary lock contention here. as an alternative, i think the rdb save routines could detect if they're in a bgsave context, and if so, don't lock at all. this introduces a small-but-real possibility of data inconsistency in a given rdb snapshot, but sidesteps the problems with this approach. thoughts?

out of memory handling in mqttasync client out of memory handling in mqttasync client migrated from bugzilla 444229 status assigned severity normal in component mqtt-c for 1.2 reported in version 1.0 on platform pc assigned to: ian craggs on 2014-09-16 06:20:32 -0400, ian craggs wrote: null checks there are no null checks on malloc. the current implementation will end up with segmentation faults on low memory situations. i assume this is not uncommon on small devices. null checks for malloc are handled in heap.c. the malloc call is overridden. this will result in error messages in the trace. looking into heap.c reveals that this code is aware of oom situations and reacts appropriately. so heap.c may return null to the mqttasync.c where no check happens. however, the question is what should the action be in the case of malloc failure? i guess the best solution is that the api call returns with failure - memory error. agreed on api level. for code running in background threads it will be more complicated since it has potentially to report the oom situation to the api consumer. and if this paths also require memory then they need to be changed. however that would add considerable complexity and code for handling the error and cleaning up partially allocated memory structures. yes. oom handling is imo part of the essential complexity of any c/c++ component. on 2014-09-16 06:30:00 -0400, ian craggs wrote: out of memory handling is "essential". it's also a balance of risk vs implementation complexity - that is, what is it worth? i think that i became less motivated to handle these situations after seeing how in general java applications cope with the same situation - usually badly. however, i think there are some relatively high risk situtations here which we should cope with. while there are small data structures allocated, the biggest risk comes from topic strings and mqtt payloads, which have a maximum size of 64k and 256mb respectively. so i would suggest we cater for those situations first, and assess whether the rest are needed. there is an mqtt problem with the receipt of messages larger than we can handle - if the message is qos 1 or 2 and we close the connection because we cannot receive the message, then the server will send it again. we could receive the entire message piecemeal and then pass it incomplete to the application, but that would violate the spirit of qos 1 or 2. there is no clean solution to this, save changing the protocol (for all the small allocations which could fail, i would rather implement one global strategy rather than every individual check. using setjmp/longjmp comes to mind. but these are relatively low risk, except perhaps if we have a lot of buffered messages. the amount of buffering can be controlled by the application however.) on 2014-09-17 08:35:33 -0400, juergen denner wrote: i think the goals could be: stability a) never segfault in any case and inform the consumer. b) reach a deterministic state and try to recover. if recover is not possible the shutdown safely and refuse new api calls with a clear error message. handle oom 'appropriately' according to the mqtt protocol for oversized messages. i see the following approaches on handling oversized payloads (oversized is determined by the execution context). reject or skip the message - this seems not to be supported by the mqtt spec. is this a gap? what you name 'piecemeal' can be named streaming. streaming is a pretty common strategy in handling arbitrary data size. so the message could be either a) send partially to the receiver including a marker for the last segment. (data push). no trivial to get it right including error handling. or - b) first received to the persistence and then it could be consumed by the client, without the risk on blocking due to network (data pull). however, i don't see the relevance for this approach on small devices. consume and 'drop' the data, inform the client that an oversized message was dropped. this would at least unblock the client. (java related comments) java never segfaults on oom (at least due to java heap ; an empty c heap do crash some jvm types). java has a clear oom strategy where you normally never react directly on oom. if you take care for (runtime) exception and do a proper resource cleanup then you are normally safe. some containers recover from such situations â�� most donâ��t. on 2014-09-17 11:11:19 -0400, ian craggs wrote: java might have a clear out of memory strategy, but whenever i've tried to recover from those situations in real tests, it never worked. this was some time ago, so things might have changed. anyway that's a digression. i think a goal should also be that the fixes ought to be testable and cater for likely to happen scenarios. note that the linux man page for malloc says: by default, linux follows an optimistic memory allocation strategy. this means that when malloc() returns non-null there is no guarantee that the memory really is available. this is a really bad bug. in case it turns out that the system is out of memory, one or more processes will be killed by the infamous oom killer. in case linux is employed under circumstances where it would be less desirable to suddenly lose some randomly picked processes, and moreover the kernel version is sufficiently recent, one can switch off this overcommitting behavior using a command like: echo 2 /proc/sys/vm/overcommit memory see also the kernel documentation directory, files vm/overcommit-accounting and sysctl/vm.txt. so, we can't guarantee freedom from segfaults. goals: a) impossible in the face of os bugs. for allocation failures internal to this api, ideally yes. b) i think trying to recover is too much work for out of memory conditions for this api. unless by recovering you mean removing all the library state and requiring the application to start again. "oversized" mqtt messages. two cases: incoming and outgoing. outgoing: just return failure to the application. most likely to happen on topic or payload allocation. there could be a max message size config parameter. incoming: rejecting the message is not supported by mqtt. this is a well known requirement for improvement. skipping the message is not allowed for qos 1 or 2. it is allowed for qos 0. i think streaming or fragmentation is over complicated for the goals of this api. not strictly allowed by the mqtt specification. the only strictly allowed action for a message to big to be received when the qos 0, is to close the session. but also in the case of qos 0, this will result in the message being sent again, unless we have connected or will connect with clean session = true. given the likelihood of occurrence vs cost of implementation i suggest this approach: deal with incoming over-sized topics/payloads by closing the connection when memory allocation failures are detected, with an appropriate reason code to connectionlost. deal with outgoing "over-sized" topics/payloads by returning memory allocation error to the application. for any other situations, allocating small data structures in the depths of a function, i think cleaning up the api state entirely and requiring the application to start again is the best option. all memory can be freed using the heap tracking routines. but i rate this as a relatively low priority because of the low likelihood of occurrence, and low likelihood of recovery. on 2014-09-24 02:51:37 -0400, juergen denner wrote: yes, malloc on linux has a really wired behavior. however - malloc for windows returns null in oom situations. at least for this platform segfaults can be avoided. comments for goals: 1b) a valid way for me is to free the paho client and create a new one. however it must be detectable by the error code. 2) many thanks for detailing this out on way of reducing the used memory for outgoing messages could be that the implementation does not create a copy of the topic & payload (maybe by an additional publish/send api) if the consumer creates the message structure using the malloc functions from the paho client then the contract would be to hand over the memory ownership to the pahoclient which releases the memory (payload, topic name) after processing. comments on your suggested approach: 1 & 2 yes 3) requiring the application to start again â�¦ do you mean destroying and recreating the pahoclient or do you mean the whole process that is using the paho client? on 2015-01-19 11:52:38 -0500, ian craggs wrote: moving to later milestone
